question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin A:**
 
• This vitamin is crucial for maintaining the health of both your skin and eyes.
 
• It is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays an essential role in ensuring normal vision.
 
• It produces pigments in the retina of the eye and promotes good vision, especially in low light.
 
• It also helps the heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs function properly.
 
• Moreover, it is involved in the regulation of the immune system.
 
• For the skin, vitamin A helps to speed up healing, prevent breakouts, and support the skin's immune system, promoting natural moisturising.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Vitamin
 Role in Skin Health
 Role in Eye Health
 
 

 Vitamin C
 As an antioxidant, helps to protect the skin from damaging free radicals caused by UV exposure. Aids in the skin's natural regeneration process and helps prevent dry skin.
 Supports the health of blood vessels in the eye and might decrease the risk of cataracts.
 
 

 Vitamin D
 May contribute to skin health by managing the growth of cells and reducing inflammation.
 Some research points to vitamin D deficiency being associated with an increased risk of age-related macular degeneration, but its role in eye health is less established.
 
 

 
 Vitamin B (B3, B5, B7, B2, B6, B9, B12)

 

 

 

 
 
 B3 and B5 improve skin hydration, reduce redness and inflammation, and boost skin elasticity. B7 promotes healthy hair, skin, and nails. 
 B2 helps prevent cataracts. A combination of B6, B9, and B12 might reduce the risk of age-related macular degeneration.
